**Marcello Hernandez** (born August 19, 1997)[1][2] is an American stand-up comedian, actor, and writer. Hernandez joined the cast of the NBC sketch comedy series *Saturday Night Live* as a featured player before the start of the show's 48th season in 2022.[3]



## Biography

[edit]

Hernandez grew up in Miami, Florida, where he attended Belen Jesuit Preparatory School. He graduated from John Carroll University in 2019 with a degree in Entrepreneurship and Communication.[4] He is of Cuban descent on his mother's side and Dominican descent on his father's side.[5]


He moved to New York City in 2019 to pursue his stand-up career.[6] In 2022, he was selected for Just for Laughs New Face of Comedy.[7][8]


Hernandez had previously done comedy and performed short-form pieces on social media channels, such as the weekly review show *Only in Dade* about his home of Miami, Florida on TikTok.[9]

## Biography

[edit]

Hernandez grew up in Miami, Florida, where he attended Belen Jesuit Preparatory School. He graduated from John Carroll University in 2019 with a degree in Entrepreneurship and Communication.[4] He is of Cuban descent on his mother's side and Dominican descent on his father's side.[5]


He moved to New York City in 2019 to pursue his stand-up career.[6] In 2022, he was selected for Just for Laughs New Face of Comedy.[7][8]

**Chloe Eileen Troast** (born 1997)[1] is an American comedian and actress. In October 2023, after four years of performing improv and stand-up comedy in New York, Troast was hired to join the cast of the NBC sketch comedy series *Saturday Night Live* for its 49th season, becoming the only new featured player for that year.




## Early life and education

[edit]

Troast was raised in Ho-Ho-Kus, New Jersey.[2] She attended New York University, where she got an individualized major at Gallatin School of Individualized Study (which she describes as "basically just an English degree") and a minor in Middle Eastern Islamic studies.[2] She sang at her college graduation.[3]



## Career

[edit]

Troast has performed improv, stand-up, and sketch comedy in New York City, sometimes embodying an Old Hollywood character named Pepper Slit.[3] Troast co-wrote and starred in the web series on *The Basics* (2021).[4] In 2023, she participated in the Montreal comedy festival Just for Laughs and was named one of its 2023 New Faces of Comedy.[3]


She has frequently collaborated with the comedy trio Please Don't Destroy (writers at *Saturday Night Live*) and will be featured in their upcoming film *Please Don't Destroy: The Treasure of Foggy Mountain*.[3][5] She is also set to appear in the romantic comedy film *Sweethearts* along with Kiernan Shipka,[3] and on the Adult Swim Smalls series *Dohl's.*[4]


After auditioning and coming close to joining the cast the previous season,[6][7] Troast made her *Saturday Night Live* debut on October 14, 2023.[2][8]



## Personal life

[edit]

Troast lives in Brooklyn, New York.[2] She enjoys crocheting.[2]

## Biography

[edit]

Hernandez grew up in Miami, Florida, where he attended Belen Jesuit Preparatory School. He graduated from John Carroll University in 2019 with a degree in Entrepreneurship and Communication.[4] He is of Cuban descent on his mother's side and Dominican descent on his father's side.[5]

## Life and career

[edit]

Longfellow was born and raised in Phoenix, Arizona. His mother and divorce attorney father later divorced; Longfellow's comedy includes references to the fact that both his parents have remarried often, resulting in a collection of stepparents.


During his first year at Arizona State University, where he earned a BA in English literature, Longfellow started performing stand-up comedy.[2] After his 2016 graduation, he moved to Los Angeles,[3] and started performing in comedy clubs across the country, as well as at the Netflix Is A Joke festival during its "Netflix Introducing..." showcase.[4] He has also appeared on *Conan* and the NBC reality competition series *Bring the Funny*, co-hosted by his future *SNL* colleague, Kenan Thompson.


In 2022, it was announced that Longfellow would be joining the cast of *Saturday Night Live* (*SNL*) as a featured player for its 48th season.[5] On October 1, 2022, Longfellow made his *SNL* debut as a new featured cast member. In his first episode, he appeared on *Weekend Update* to discuss anti-vaccination relatives and actress Sydney Sweeney’s Trump-supporting family members.[6]

**Chloe Eileen Troast** (born 1997)[1] is an American comedian and actress. In October 2023, after four years of performing improv and stand-up comedy in New York, Troast was hired to join the cast of the NBC sketch comedy series *Saturday Night Live* for its 49th season, becoming the only new featured player for that year.




## Early life and education

[edit]

Troast was raised in Ho-Ho-Kus, New Jersey.[2] She attended New York University, where she got an individualized major at Gallatin School of Individualized Study (which she describes as "basically just an English degree") and a minor in Middle Eastern Islamic studies.[2] She sang at her college graduation.[3]



## Career

[edit]

Troast has performed improv, stand-up, and sketch comedy in New York City, sometimes embodying an Old Hollywood character named Pepper Slit.[3] Troast co-wrote and starred in the web series on *The Basics* (2021).[4] In 2023, she participated in the Montreal comedy festival Just for Laughs and was named one of its 2023 New Faces of Comedy.[3]


She has frequently collaborated with the comedy trio Please Don't Destroy (writers at *Saturday Night Live*) and will be featured in their upcoming film *Please Don't Destroy: The Treasure of Foggy Mountain*.[3][5] She is also set to appear in the romantic comedy film *Sweethearts* along with Kiernan Shipka,[3] and on the Adult Swim Smalls series *Dohl's.*[4]


After auditioning and coming close to joining the cast the previous season,[6][7] Troast made her *Saturday Night Live* debut on October 14, 2023.[2][8]



## Personal life

[edit]

Troast lives in Brooklyn, New York.[2] She enjoys crocheting.[2]

**Chloe Eileen Troast** (born 1997)[1] is an American comedian and actress. In October 2023, after four years of performing improv and stand-up comedy in New York, Troast was hired to join the cast of the NBC sketch comedy series *Saturday Night Live* for its 49th season, becoming the only new featured player for that year.




## Early life and education

[edit]

Troast was raised in Ho-Ho-Kus, New Jersey.[2] She attended New York University, where she got an individualized major at Gallatin School of Individualized Study (which she describes as "basically just an English degree") and a minor in Middle Eastern Islamic studies.[2] She sang at her college graduation.[3]



## Career

[edit]

Troast has performed improv, stand-up, and sketch comedy in New York City, sometimes embodying an Old Hollywood character named Pepper Slit.[3] Troast co-wrote and starred in the web series on *The Basics* (2021).[4] In 2023, she participated in the Montreal comedy festival Just for Laughs and was named one of its 2023 New Faces of Comedy.[3]


She has frequently collaborated with the comedy trio Please Don't Destroy (writers at *Saturday Night Live*) and will be featured in their upcoming film *Please Don't Destroy: The Treasure of Foggy Mountain*.[3][5] She is also set to appear in the romantic comedy film *Sweethearts* along with Kiernan Shipka,[3] and on the Adult Swim Smalls series *Dohl's.*[4]


After auditioning and coming close to joining the cast the previous season,[6][7] Troast made her *Saturday Night Live* debut on October 14, 2023.[2][8]



## Personal life

[edit]

Troast lives in Brooklyn, New York.[2] She enjoys crocheting.[2]

**Chloe Eileen Troast** (born 1997)[1] is an American comedian and actress. In October 2023, after four years of performing improv and stand-up comedy in New York, Troast was hired to join the cast of the NBC sketch comedy series *Saturday Night Live* for its 49th season, becoming the only new featured player for that year.




## Early life and education

[edit]

Troast was raised in Ho-Ho-Kus, New Jersey.[2] She attended New York University, where she got an individualized major at Gallatin School of Individualized Study (which she describes as "basically just an English degree") and a minor in Middle Eastern Islamic studies.[2] She sang at her college graduation.[3]



## Career

[edit]

Troast has performed improv, stand-up, and sketch comedy in New York City, sometimes embodying an Old Hollywood character named Pepper Slit.[3] Troast co-wrote and starred in the web series on *The Basics* (2021).[4] In 2023, she participated in the Montreal comedy festival Just for Laughs and was named one of its 2023 New Faces of Comedy.[3]


She has frequently collaborated with the comedy trio Please Don't Destroy (writers at *Saturday Night Live*) and will be featured in their upcoming film *Please Don't Destroy: The Treasure of Foggy Mountain*.[3][5] She is also set to appear in the romantic comedy film *Sweethearts* along with Kiernan Shipka,[3] and on the Adult Swim Smalls series *Dohl's.*[4]


After auditioning and coming close to joining the cast the previous season,[6][7] Troast made her *Saturday Night Live* debut on October 14, 2023.[2][8]



## Personal life

[edit]

Troast lives in Brooklyn, New York.[2] She enjoys crocheting.[2]

In 2022, Kearney was hired to join the cast of the NBC sketch comedy series *Saturday Night Live* as a featured player for the show's 48th season, making their debut alongside Marcello Hernandez, Michael Longfellow, and Devon Walker.


Kearney uses they/them pronouns.[4][5]

[edit]

Born and raised in Cleveland,[6] they frequently performed stand-up comedy in Chicago, later moving to Los Angeles.[4]

Kearney's screen credits include the Amazon series *A League of Their Own* and the Disney+ series *The Mighty Ducks: Game Changers*.[7][4] In 2022, they were announced as the first openly non-binary cast member of *Saturday Night Live*.[4][7][5]

## Biography

[edit]

Hernandez grew up in Miami, Florida, where he attended Belen Jesuit Preparatory School. He graduated from John Carroll University in 2019 with a degree in Entrepreneurship and Communication.[4] He is of Cuban descent on his mother's side and Dominican descent on his father's side.[5]


He moved to New York City in 2019 to pursue his stand-up career.[6] In 2022, he was selected for Just for Laughs New Face of Comedy.[7][8]

## Life and career

[edit]

Longfellow was born and raised in Phoenix, Arizona. His mother and divorce attorney father later divorced; Longfellow's comedy includes references to the fact that both his parents have remarried often, resulting in a collection of stepparents.


During his first year at Arizona State University, where he earned a BA in English literature, Longfellow started performing stand-up comedy.[2] After his 2016 graduation, he moved to Los Angeles,[3] and started performing in comedy clubs across the country, as well as at the Netflix Is A Joke festival during its "Netflix Introducing..." showcase.[4] He has also appeared on *Conan* and the NBC reality competition series *Bring the Funny*, co-hosted by his future *SNL* colleague, Kenan Thompson.


In 2022, it was announced that Longfellow would be joining the cast of *Saturday Night Live* (*SNL*) as a featured player for its 48th season.[5] On October 1, 2022, Longfellow made his *SNL* debut as a new featured cast member. In his first episode, he appeared on *Weekend Update* to discuss anti-vaccination relatives and actress Sydney Sweeney’s Trump-supporting family members.[6]

## Career

[edit]

Troast has performed improv, stand-up, and sketch comedy in New York City, sometimes embodying an Old Hollywood character named Pepper Slit.[3] Troast co-wrote and starred in the web series on *The Basics* (2021).[4] In 2023, she participated in the Montreal comedy festival Just for Laughs and was named one of its 2023 New Faces of Comedy.[3]


She has frequently collaborated with the comedy trio Please Don't Destroy (writers at *Saturday Night Live*) and will be featured in their upcoming film *Please Don't Destroy: The Treasure of Foggy Mountain*.[3][5] She is also set to appear in the romantic comedy film *Sweethearts* along with Kiernan Shipka,[3] and on the Adult Swim Smalls series *Dohl's.*[4]


After auditioning and coming close to joining the cast the previous season,[6][7] Troast made her *Saturday Night Live* debut on October 14, 2023.[2][8]



## Personal life

[edit]

Troast lives in Brooklyn, New York.[2] She enjoys crocheting.[2]
